# package server

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/server"
```

Package server is the DNP3 outstation (IEEE 1815-2012).

A [Server](#type-server) holds a [Database](#type-database) of points (binary, double-bit, counters, frozen counters, analogs, frozen analogs, outputs, octet strings) whose changes become events in classes 1 to 3, buffered per master (association) and reported in polls and unsolicited responses. Controls, restarts, time synchronization and the application functions go to the [Handler](#type-handler) of [WithHandler](#func-withhandler) and its optional interfaces; file transfer to the [FileServer](#type-fileserver) of [WithFileServer](#func-withfileserver).

Device attributes are [WithAttributes](#func-withattributes) (set 0) and [WithAttributeSet](#func-withattributeset); FREEZE\_AT\_TIME requests are scheduled (MaxScheduledFreezes).

Transports: [Server.ListenAndServe](#func-server-listenandserve) and [Server.Serve](#func-server-serve) for TCP, TLS with [WithTLS](#func-withtls), [Server.ServeUDP](#func-server-serveudp) for UDP, [Server.ServeConn](#func-server-serveconn) for any byte stream such as a serial port, and [Server.DialAndServe](#func-server-dialandserve) for the dual end point, where the outstation connects to its master. [Server.Close](#func-server-close) ends them all. A [Group](#type-group) serves several outstations, each a Server at its own link address, on the same port or line (multi-drop).

Secure Authentication version 5 ([WithSecureAuthentication](#func-withsecureauthentication)) challenges critical requests, takes part in the session key change, accepts aggressive mode requests and keeps the security statistics (g121, g122) per master.

API.md lists the whole API; INTEROPERABILITY.md what is implemented, clause by clause.

## Constants

```go
const DefaultEventLimit = 100
```

DefaultEventLimit is the number of events of each point type an association buffers when no limit is configured.

```go
const DefaultPort = 20000
```

DefaultPort is the registered DNP3 port.

```go
const DefaultReplyTimeout = 10 * time.Second
```

DefaultReplyTimeout is how long a challenge waits for its reply when SecureAuth.ReplyTimeout is zero.

```go
const MaxScheduledFreezes = 16
```

MaxScheduledFreezes is how many FREEZE\_AT\_TIME requests the outstation keeps waiting at once; a further one is refused. They belong to the Server: a periodic one keeps its place until Close, whatever happens to the master's connection.

```go
var DefaultCritical = secauth.DefaultCritical
```

DefaultCritical are the function codes challenged by default: the ones that change the outstation's state.

## Types

### type ActivateConfigHandler

```go
type ActivateConfigHandler interface {
	ActivateConfig(ctx context.Context, headers []app.Header) (app.ActivateConfigStatus, app.IIN)
}
```

ActivateConfigHandler is an optional interface of the [Handler](#type-handler) for ACTIVATE\_CONFIG (function code 31). When the handler implements it, ACTIVATE\_CONFIG goes to ActivateConfig instead of [ApplicationHandler](#type-applicationhandler).

headers are the request's objects: file specifications (g70v8, as app.FileSpecification) or octet strings (g110) that name the configurations to activate. ActivateConfig returns the status of requested operation and the IIN2 error bits of the response. Without an error bit the response carries the status in one g91v1 object with qualifier 0x07 (count 1); with one, the response has no object. A status that does not encode (app.ActivateConfigStatus.Raw) or does not fit the largest response fragment is answered with IIN2.2 (PARAMETER\_ERROR).

### type ApplicationHandler

```go
type ApplicationHandler interface {
	Application(ctx context.Context, fc app.FunctionCode, headers []app.Header) app.IIN
}
```

ApplicationHandler is an optional interface of the [Handler](#type-handler) for the function codes that act on the outstation's applications: INITIALIZE\_DATA, INITIALIZE\_APPL, START\_APPL, STOP\_APPL, SAVE\_CONFIG and ACTIVATE\_CONFIG. It returns the IIN2 error bits of the response; 0 is success. Without it these functions are answered with IIN2.0.

### type Group

```go
type Group struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Group serves several outstations on the same connections: a multi-drop channel (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 9), where every station takes the frames to its own link address and all of them the broadcasts. Each outstation is a [Server](#type-server) with its own address, database, handler and options; the group only shares the listeners and connections, so that a master reaches each by its address over one port or one serial line.

#### func NewGroup

```go
func NewGroup(servers ...*Server) (*Group, error)
```

NewGroup returns a group of servers, which must have distinct addresses. The servers are served through the group: do not serve them on their own as well.

#### func (Group) Close

```go
func (g *Group) Close() error
```

Close stops the listeners and closes every server of the group, and with them the connections.

#### func (Group) ListenAndServe

```go
func (g *Group) ListenAndServe(addr string) error
```

ListenAndServe listens on the TCP address addr (":20000" when empty), with the TLS configuration of the first server's WithTLS when it has one, and serves until Close.

#### func (Group) Serve

```go
func (g *Group) Serve(l net.Listener) error
```

Serve accepts connections on l and serves each until Close. A connection is refused while the group holds as many as the smallest WithMaxConnections of its servers. It returns nil after Close, otherwise the error that stopped the listener.

#### func (Group) ServeConn

```go
func (g *Group) ServeConn(rw io.ReadWriteCloser, remote net.Addr) error
```

ServeConn serves one stream, for example a serial port, for every outstation of the group until it ends or the group is closed.

#### func (Group) ServeUDP

```go
func (g *Group) ServeUDP(pc net.PacketConn) error
```

ServeUDP serves the outstations of the group over UDP on pc, as [Server.ServeUDP](#func-server-serveudp) does for one.

#### func (Group) Servers

```go
func (g *Group) Servers() []*Server
```

Servers returns the servers of the group, in the order given.

### type Handler

```go
type Handler interface {
	// Select checks whether the control could be executed now, without
	// executing it.
	Select(ctx context.Context, c Command) app.CommandStatus

	// Operate executes the control.
	Operate(ctx context.Context, c Command, op OperateType) app.CommandStatus
}
```

Handler executes controls. Its methods are called on the goroutine of the master's association, one request at a time per master; a slow handler delays that master's requests, not the others'.

The returned status is echoed to the master. A handler that does not support a point returns app.StatusNotSupported; the response then also sets IIN2.2 (PARAMETER\_ERROR).

### type Option

```go
type Option func(*options) error
```

Option configures a [Server](#type-server).

#### func WithAddress

```go
func WithAddress(a link.Address) Option
```

WithAddress sets the link address of the outstation. The default is 10.

#### func WithAttributeSet

```go
func WithAttributeSet(set uint16, attrs map[uint8]app.Attribute, writable ...uint8) Option
```

WithAttributeSet sets the device attributes of another set (group 0, the set is the index; IEEE 1815-2012 clause 11.9.1), keyed by variation. The variations in writable can be written by a master, with a value of the same type: the outstation stores it and, when the [Handler](#type-handler) implements [AttributeSetWriteHandler](#type-attributesetwritehandler), tells it first. Other writes are refused.

#### func WithAttributes

```go
func WithAttributes(attrs map[uint8]app.Attribute) Option
```

WithAttributes sets the device attributes of set 0 (group 0) the outstation reports, keyed by variation, for example app.AttrManufacturerName. The list of attribute variations (g0v255) is built from them; an attribute is writable when the [Handler](#type-handler) implements [WriteHandler](#type-writehandler).

#### func WithConfirmTimeout

```go
func WithConfirmTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithConfirmTimeout sets how long the outstation waits for the application confirmation of a response or unsolicited response. The default is 5 seconds.

#### func WithEventLimits

```go
func WithEventLimits(limits map[PointType]int) Option
```

WithEventLimits sets the number of events of each point type an association buffers; types not named keep DefaultEventLimit. When a buffer is full the oldest event of the type is discarded and the outstation reports IIN2.3 (EVENT\_BUFFER\_OVERFLOW).

#### func WithFileServer

```go
func WithFileServer(fs FileServer) Option
```

WithFileServer serves file transfer (group 70) from fs.

#### func WithHandler

```go
func WithHandler(h Handler) Option
```

WithHandler sets the handler for controls and, through its optional interfaces, for restarts, time synchronization, application functions and writes. The default supports no control.

#### func WithLink

```go
func WithLink(l Link) Option
```

WithLink configures the data link layer.

#### func WithLogger

```go
func WithLogger(l dnp3.Logger) Option
```

WithLogger sets the logger; logging is silent by default.

#### func WithMasters

```go
func WithMasters(addrs ...link.Address) Option
```

WithMasters restricts the masters the outstation answers to these link addresses. Their associations, and so their event buffers, exist from the start: events are kept while a master is not connected. Without it any master is answered and its association is created on first contact.

#### func WithMaxConnections

```go
func WithMaxConnections(n int) Option
```

WithMaxConnections limits concurrent connections; further ones are closed at once. The default is 16.

#### func WithMaxControls

```go
func WithMaxControls(n int) Option
```

WithMaxControls sets how many controls one request may carry; the controls beyond it are answered with TOO\_MANY\_OBJS. The default is 16.

#### func WithMaxFragment

```go
func WithMaxFragment(tx, rx int) Option
```

WithMaxFragment sets the largest response fragment the outstation sends (tx) and the largest request it reassembles (rx). The defaults are 2048; IEEE 1815-2012 requires at least 249.

#### func WithMetrics

```go
func WithMetrics(m dnp3.Metrics) Option
```

WithMetrics sets the metrics callbacks. A value that also implements dnp3.ServerMetrics receives the server-level callbacks.

#### func WithSecureAuthentication

```go
func WithSecureAuthentication(sa SecureAuth) Option
```

WithSecureAuthentication enables Secure Authentication: critical requests are executed only after the master answered a challenge with the right MAC, or when they carry it themselves in aggressive mode. The outstation takes part in the session key change and keeps the security statistics (g121, g122) per master. A user number of 0, which IEEE 1815-2012 reserves for an unknown user, is taken as 1, the default user.

#### func WithSelectTimeout

```go
func WithSelectTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithSelectTimeout sets how long a SELECT stays valid for its OPERATE; an OPERATE after it is answered with TIMEOUT. The default is 10 seconds.

#### func WithSelfAddress

```go
func WithSelfAddress(enabled bool) Option
```

WithSelfAddress makes the outstation accept frames sent to the self address 0xFFFC as if they were sent to its own address.

#### func WithTLS

```go
func WithTLS(cfg *tls.Config) Option
```

WithTLS serves TLS (IEEE 1815-2012 Annex B / IEC 62351-3) on the listeners of ListenAndServe, and is the TLS client configuration of DialAndServe. Serve and ServeConn take the connection as it is.

#### func WithTimeSync

```go
func WithTimeSync(interval time.Duration) Option
```

WithTimeSync makes the outstation request time synchronization (IIN1.4 NEED\_TIME) at start and again when interval has passed since the last one. Zero, the default, never requests it.

Its time counts as unsynchronized, which relative-time events report with a g51v2 CTO instead of g51v1, until the first synchronization after the start or a restart, and again once twice the interval has passed without one.

#### func WithUnsolicited

```go
func WithUnsolicited(u Unsolicited) Option
```

WithUnsolicited configures unsolicited responses; they are disabled by default.

### type PointConfig

```go
type PointConfig struct {
	// Class is the event class, 0..3. Events are only produced for 1..3.
	Class Class

	// StaticVariation is the variation of the point in class 0 and in
	// reads of "any variation"; 0 selects the type's default (g1v2, g3v2,
	// g10v2, g20v1, g21v1, g30v1, g31v1, g40v1).
	StaticVariation uint8

	// EventVariation is the variation of the point's events; 0 selects
	// the default (g2v2, g4v2, g11v2, g22v5, g23v5, g32v3, g33v3, g42v3).
	EventVariation uint8

	// Deadband applies to counters, frozen counters and analog points: a
	// change of the value produces an event only when it exceeds the
	// deadband. Flag changes always produce one. It must be a finite number
	// of at least zero; Add refuses NaN, infinity and negative deadbands, and
	// a WRITE of one is answered with IIN2.2.
	Deadband float64

	// ExcludeFromClass0 leaves the point out of class 0 responses; it can
	// still be read by group and variation.
	ExcludeFromClass0 bool

	// CommandEventClass, for binary and analog outputs, reports every
	// OPERATE, DIRECT_OPERATE and DIRECT_OPERATE_NR of the point as a
	// command event in that class: g13 (the commanded state) or g43 (the
	// commanded value) with the status the handler returned. 0 reports
	// none.
	CommandEventClass Class

	// CommandEventVariation is the variation of the command events; 0
	// selects g13v2 or g43v3 (with time).
	CommandEventVariation uint8
}
```

PointConfig configures one point.

	// SecurityStatistic are the Secure Authentication statistics (group

	// (groups 13 and 43) of the outputs whose PointConfig has a
	// CommandEventClass. They have no static objects and cannot be added

	BinaryOutputCommand
	AnalogOutputCommand
	// TimeAndInterval are indexed absolute times with an interval (g50v4,
	// app.AbsoluteTime with Units), for example a schedule. They have no
	// events and no class.
	TimeAndInterval
)
```

type SecureAuth struct {

}
```

SecureAuth configures DNP3 Secure Authentication version 5 (see package secauth): with an update key, the master negotiates the session keys with the session key change; without, a pre-shared session key is used.

### type Server

```go
type Server struct {

	// scheduled FREEZE_AT_TIME

}
```

Server is a DNP3 outstation: a point database served to masters over any number of channels.

#### func New

```go
func New(opts ...Option) (*Server, error)
```

New returns an outstation configured by opts. Add points to its Database, then serve it with ListenAndServe, Serve or ServeConn.

#### func (Server) Address

```go
func (s *Server) Address() link.Address
```

Address returns the link address of the outstation.

#### func (Server) Close

```go
func (s *Server) Close() error
```

Close stops the listeners, closes every connection and stops the associations. It waits for their goroutines to end.

#### func (Server) CloseConnections

```go
func (s *Server) CloseConnections()
```

CloseConnections closes every current client connection without stopping the listeners: masters may reconnect. Associations and their event buffers are kept.

#### func (Server) Database

```go
func (s *Server) Database() *Database
```

Database returns the point database.

#### func (Server) DialAndServe

```go
func (s *Server) DialAndServe(ctx context.Context, addr string, r Redial) error
```

DialAndServe is the outstation's end of a TCP connection that the outstation establishes (the dual end point of IEEE 1815-2012 annex A.3, for an outstation behind a firewall or on a dial-out link): it connects to the master at addr, with TLS when WithTLS was given (the outstation is then the TLS client: the configuration's RootCAs verify the master, its Certificates are presented, ServerName defaults to the host of addr), serves the connection like an accepted one, and connects again when it ends, with the delays of r. It returns when ctx is done (ctx.Err()) or the server is closed (nil).

#### func (Server) ListenAndServe

```go
func (s *Server) ListenAndServe(addr string) error
```

ListenAndServe listens on the TCP address addr (":20000" when empty), with TLS when WithTLS was given, and serves until Close.

#### func (Server) Now

```go
func (s *Server) Now() time.Time
```

Now returns the time of the outstation's clock, which time synchronization sets.

#### func (Server) Restart

```go
func (s *Server) Restart()
```

Restart behaves as after a restart of the outstation: every association reports IIN1.7 (DEVICE\_RESTART) again, its event buffer is cleared, unsolicited responses start over with a null unsolicited response, and, with WithTimeSync, its time counts as unsynchronized until the next time synchronization (IIN1.4).

#### func (Server) Serve

```go
func (s *Server) Serve(l net.Listener) error
```

Serve accepts connections on l and serves each until Close. It returns nil after Close, otherwise the error that stopped the listener.

#### func (Server) ServeConn

```go
func (s *Server) ServeConn(rw io.ReadWriteCloser, remote net.Addr) error
```

ServeConn serves one stream, for example a serial port or a connection accepted elsewhere, until it ends or the server is closed. remote names the peer in logs and metrics and may be nil. It returns the reason the stream ended: nil after Close.

#### func (Server) ServeUDP

```go
func (s *Server) ServeUDP(pc net.PacketConn) error
```

ServeUDP serves DNP3 over UDP on pc until Close. Each datagram carries link frames; responses go to the address the last datagram came from, so one socket serves one master at a time (a master behind another address takes over the socket when it sends).

Until a master has sent a datagram there is nowhere to send to: what the outstation sends before (the null unsolicited response, for one) is dropped, as an unreachable datagram would be, and repeated by the unsolicited retries. Use ServeUDPTo to name the master's address up front.

#### func (Server) ServeUDPTo

```go
func (s *Server) ServeUDPTo(pc net.PacketConn, peer net.Addr) error
```

ServeUDPTo is ServeUDP with the master's address known from the start: unsolicited responses reach it before it sent anything. A datagram from another address takes over the socket, as with ServeUDP.

#### func (Server) SetIndications

```go
func (s *Server) SetIndications(bits app.IIN, on bool)
```

SetIndications sets or clears the application controlled internal indications of every association: app.IINLocalControl, app.IINDeviceTrouble and app.IINConfigCorrupt. Other bits are ignored.

### type TimeHandler

```go
type TimeHandler interface {
	SetTime(ctx context.Context, t time.Time)
}
```

TimeHandler is an optional interface of the [Handler](#type-handler). The outstation keeps its own clock, set by time synchronization; a TimeHandler is told of every synchronization as well, for example to set the device clock.

### type Unsolicited

```go
type Unsolicited struct {
	// Enabled allows unsolicited responses. When set, the outstation sends
	// a null unsolicited response when a master connects and reports
	// events of the classes the master enables (or of Classes from the
	// start).
	Enabled bool
	// Classes are the classes (1..3) enabled before any ENABLE_UNSOLICITED,
	// IEEE 1815-2012's "unsolicited allowed at startup".
	Classes []Class
	// HoldTime is how long new events are collected before they are sent
	// unsolicited. Zero sends at once.
	HoldTime time.Duration
	// HoldCount sends at once when this many events are pending, before
	// HoldTime has passed. Zero means no count trigger.
	HoldCount int
	// Retries is how often an unconfirmed unsolicited response is
	// repeated before it is given up; its events are kept and reported
	// later. Zero means 3; a negative value repeats it until it is
	// confirmed.
	Retries int
	// RetryDelay is the pause after an unsolicited response was given up.
	// Zero means 5 seconds.
	RetryDelay time.Duration
}
```

Unsolicited configures unsolicited responses.

### type WriteHandler

```go
type WriteHandler interface {
	WriteAttribute(ctx context.Context, variation uint8, a app.Attribute) error
	WriteOctetString(ctx context.Context, index uint32, data []byte) error
}
```

WriteHandler is an optional interface of the [Handler](#type-handler) for WRITE requests on objects the outstation does not handle itself: device attributes (group 0) and octet strings (group 110). The outstation stores a written octet string in its database before it calls WriteOctetString. Errors are answered with IIN2.2 (PARAMETER\_ERROR).
